info.title: Stablevoy API
info.description:
Stablevoy accepts USDC and USDT payments that go straight to your own wallet. This reference lists every endpoint; the guides (payment flow, webhooks, WooCommerce, recovery) are at https://stablevoy.com/docs/.

## Authentication

- **API key** for your server and plugins: `Authorization: Bearer sk_live_...`. Create keys in the dashboard, one store per key. Never put a key in a browser or an app.
- **Merchant session** for the dashboard and apps: Sign-In with Ethereum (`/v1/auth/siwe/*`). Browsers get httpOnly cookies, apps get a bearer token.

## Amounts

Invoice amounts are integers in US cents (`1999` is $19.99). Token amounts are strings in the token's smallest units (USDC and USDT have 6 decimals on most networks), so large values never lose precision.

## Idempotency

Send an `Idempotency-Key` header when creating an invoice (your order id is a good key). Retrying with the same key and body returns the first invoice with `replayed: true` instead of a duplicate.

## Pagination

List endpoints take `limit` (1 to 100) and return `nextCursor`; pass it as `cursor` until it is `null`.

## Errors

Errors are RFC 7807 problem documents (`application/problem+json`) with a stable `code`, a readable `detail` and a `type` link to the code's entry in the error catalog: https://stablevoy.com/docs/api/errors/.

## Maintenance

During maintenance the API answers every request with `503`, code `maintenance` and a `Retry-After` header, before the request reaches it, so nothing is changed. Retry after the given time. Payments sent on chain meanwhile are safe and are credited afterwards.

## Webhooks

Stablevoy POSTs invoice events to the store's webhook URL, signed with HMAC-SHA256. How to verify them: https://stablevoy.com/docs/#webhooks.

Only for an invoice that still waits for a payment and is offered on that Tron network. The answer is checked against the invoice before it is returned, and the payment page decodes rawDataHex itself before the wallet is asked to sign it.
